title: Oceanic Anoxic Event 1a (Selli Event)
summary: Oceanic Anoxic Event 1a, the Selli Event, occurred in the early Aptian about 120 million years ago and lasted roughly 1.1 million years in one study (1.3 million in another). It is recorded globally in marine deposits as organic-rich black shale from widespread oxygen deficiency, with a 2.7 per mil negative carbon-isotope shift at La Frontera, Spain; volcanogenic CO2 from large igneous provinces is the proposed driver.

uncertainty.note: Start is "ca. 120 Ma" (Bottini et al. 2021; Herdocia and Maurrasse 2025). End adds the ca. 1.1 Myr duration stated by Bottini et al.; Herdocia and Maurrasse use 1.3 Ma. Years are Ma with no 1950 offset.

when.display: c. 120 million years ago (lasting c. 1.1 Myr)

where.modern_name: Cismon Core site near Cismon del Grappa, northern Italy (western Tethys reference section for a global event)
where.historical_name: Lombardy Basin, western Tethys; no polities

importance.justification: A major Cretaceous carbon-cycle and ocean-deoxygenation event with widespread black shales.
